_about: Each legislature's fixed facts for the balance of power (balance.py): seats in each chamber (S = Senate, the state's lower-house letter otherwise), the share of each house's seats it takes to override a veto ("majority": more than half, as in Indiana), and the governor serving now with their party. Party seat counts aren't here: they come from each session's member list. Update `governor` when a new one takes office (also GOVERNORS in the state's profile.py); `coalition` lists chambers a bipartisan coalition runs (Alaska's: no party controls them, whatever the seat counts say); `note` says what seat counts alone don't (a bipartisan coalition running a chamber, an officially nonpartisan legislature). Checked 2026-11-07.

ak.note: Bipartisan coalitions run both houses in 2025–26: in the House, 14 Democrats, 5 independents and 2 Republicans (Speaker Bryce Edgmon is an independent); in the Senate, 9 Democrats and 5 Republicans (President Gary Stevens is a Republican). Overriding a veto takes the two houses meeting together: 40 of the 60 legislators, or 45 for an appropriation bill.

id.note: Overriding a veto takes two-thirds of the members present in each house.

me.note: The House also seats two tribal representatives (the Passamaquoddy Tribe's and the Houlton Band of Maliseet Indians'), who don't vote on the floor. Overriding a veto takes two-thirds of the members present in each house.

ok.note: Overriding a veto of a bill with an emergency clause takes three-fourths of each house (36 senators, 76 representatives).

ri.note: Overriding a veto takes three-fifths of the members present and voting in each house.

vt.note: Overriding a veto takes two-thirds of the members present in each house. Progressives who also run as Democrats are counted with the Democrats.
